common.help_desc: What the abbreviations, alert levels and cloud levels mean
common.help_ghi: Global horizontal irradiance in W/m²: the higher it is, the more the panels generate
common.help_pgen: Forecast power = panel area × efficiency × GHI ÷ 1000 (kW), from the GHI that blends the LSTM with the satellite
common.help_ptarget: The highest power the station has to deliver by plan (kW), set by the administrator. The target at a given time is the smaller of P_target and 80% of the clear-sky output at that time, so it is lower in the morning and evening.
common.help_dp: The largest amount by which P_gen falls below the target of that time within the next 3 hours (kW); 0 when the target is met throughout
common.help_reserve: Reserve to hold = ΔP plus a buffer for the model's forecast error
common.help_lstm: Model that forecasts GHI 3 hours ahead from the recent weather data
common.help_convlstm: Model that predicts the next 18 satellite frames. The first 30 minutes use what the newest real frame shows, after 90 minutes the model's forecast, and a mix in between. Without a complete 12-frame window only the newest real frame is used.
common.help_ghi_blend: Blend = LSTM weighted with the satellite result. The satellite weighs more at short lead times (about 80% at 10 min, 50% at 1 hour) and less later.
common.help_cloud: Cloud cover = cloudy pixels ÷ all pixels in the 5×5 px box around the station (about 78×55 km). The impact level comes from the expected loss of light.
common.help_alert_night: The sun is down, there is no generation; not an alert
common.help_alert_normal: The target is met for 3 hours and the cloud impact is low
common.help_alert_watch: The target is met but the cloud impact is medium: keep watching
common.help_alert_warning: Power will fall below the target, or the target is met but the cloud impact is high: prepare reserve
common.help_alert_critical: Power will fall below the target and the cloud impact is high: dispatch reserve now
common.help_cloud_method: The expected loss of light comes from the mean brightness of the satellite image in the box around the station, with a relation fitted on measured GHI (k = a − b × brightness): the brighter the box, the less light reaches the ground.

The white box is the 5×5 px area around the station. Orange flags are hints from the system; they do not reject a frame by themselves.
